statements.t: Additionally, uncertainty related to changes in tariffs, trade restrictions and policies, legislation, and guidance, including from H.R.1, and proposed regulations in Germany that may negatively impact feed-in tariffs, may contribute to growing market volatility and adversely impact customer demand for our products, pricing and our financial performance.
We expect the softness in demand to continue in the fourth quarter of 2026 and there can be no assurance that our sales will not further decrease.

In August 2022, the U.S. government enacted the IRA, which contains several provisions intended to accelerate U.S. manufacturing and adoption of clean energy such as solar, wind, hydrogen and electric vehicles and therefore had positive impacts on our business and operations along with the overall U.S. solar market.

However, if the Treasury were to release new rules or guidance that impact our ability to provide components with non-PFE percentages towards their total requirement, our customers’ eligibility to qualify for certain tax credits could be impaired, which may adversely affect our revenue, gross margins, business operations and competitive position.

However, if the Treasury guidance relating to the calculation of non-PFE content should change in a way that would impact our ability to reach that required percentage, it could have adverse impacts on our manufacturing costs, results of operations, cash flows, gross margin, and profits.
On August 15, 2025, the Treasury and the IRS released Notice 2025-42, its first set of guidance for H.R.1 related to the beginning of construction requirements applicable to our customers.
This guidance provides answers to several compliance questions related to our AMPTC material assistance calculations and its customers’ 48E material assistance calculation among other things.
Such future regulations or guidance could affect the determination of our eligibility for AMPTCs and our customers’ eligibility for Sections 45Y and 48E credits.

To the extent that tax benefits or credits may be impacted through new regulation, issued guidance, interpretation, or by new laws passed by Congress, our business could be disadvantaged or advantaged.

If tariffs or other trade measures increase the cost of our products or other components of solar power systems, solar power systems could become less economically attractive, which could reduce demand for our products and adversely affect our gross margins.
If enacted as proposed, reduced feed-in tariff support could lower demand for new residential solar installations in Germany and, as a result, for our products.
We cannot predict whether, when or in what form the proposed legislation will be adopted or its ultimate effect on our business.
We plan to pursue additional tax credit sales in the future.
We intend to use the remainder of the net proceeds from the Notes 2029 Offering for general corporate purposes.
